author: @HeisDulaa
comment:
The hook of the video "World’s Deadliest Obstacle Course!" is engaging and attention-grabbing. Here is an analysis of what is good and how it can be improved:

What is good:
1) The hook sets up a high-stakes situation with the mention of the most deadly obstacle course in the world and the risk of falling 200 feet to the ground.
2) The introduction of the friend, Mack, who is attempting the course adds a personal element to the story.
3) The use of descriptive language like "absolutely insane" and "deadly, painful" creates a sense of danger and excitement.
4) The promise of a significant reward ($800,000) for completing the obstacle courses adds a compelling incentive for viewers to keep watching.

How it can be improved:
1) The hook could benefit from a more concise and punchy delivery to grab viewers' attention immediately within the first few seconds.
2) Including a quick preview of some of the obstacles Mack will face could increase curiosity and anticipation for what's to come.
3) Adding a quick teaser of some of the most challenging moments or close calls Mack will experience could heighten suspense and keep viewers hooked.

Overall, the hook is strong in setting up the premise and stakes of the video, but could be enhanced by tightening the delivery and providing a sneak peek of the upcoming challenges.

Hello MrBeast!

First of all, I wanted to thank you for all the things you do for people with disabilities, those in need, and everyone around the world!

I am writing these few lines to explain my situation, and I must confess that while writing this message, I already have tears in my eyes and a heavy heart.

You should know that I come from a large family; we settled in France, and my parents did everything so that we didn't lack anything. To make them proud, I tried to work hard at school. I completed a scientific baccalaureate with the aim of becoming a pilot, but for various reasons, I couldn't change my life and achieve this goal. So, I turned to nursing studies, and I strive every day to take care of my patients, especially in oncology, to support them until they return home or in their end-of-life journey. But I must admit that it is very tough psychologically, and I often think about aviation and the dream that still haunts me.

Today, I visited a school that I really liked, but the cost is very high. I can't afford to pay for the school or the accommodation. It's a dream that I find hard to let go of—becoming a pilot has always been my dream.

I know that my message is one among millions of messages that you receive, and my hope is so great that I am placing it among your many messages.

Thank you for reading my message, hoping that one day you will see it and be able to help me.
